caption_en:
Perfect quality of life: 100. Israel: 92.

The UN's Human Development Index combines health, education and income. Israel: 0.919, 27th in the world (Human Development Report 2025, 2023 data).

What's in the gap?
• Poverty: 20.7% of Israelis (National Insurance Institute).
• Prices: 4th highest of the 38 OECD countries (OECD 2025).
• Rank: 27th. Iceland is 1st (0.972).

Zoom out, same scale (x100): 🇦🇪 UAE 94, 🇮🇱 Israel 92, 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia 90, 🇹🇷 Turkey 85, 🇮🇷 Iran 80, 🇯🇴 Jordan 75, 🇪🇬 Egypt 75, 🇱🇧 Lebanon 75. The UN's average for medium development: 66.

Honest catch: the UAE beats Israel, 15th in the world.

We're not perfect. But poor and backward? Not even close.

Send this to a critic.
caption_he:
איכות חיים מושלמת: 100. ישראל: 92, מקום 27 בעולם במדד הפיתוח האנושי של האו"ם.
בפער: עוני (20.7%), יוקר מחיה (מקום 4 מתוך 38 במדינות ה־OECD), ואיסלנד במקום הראשון.
זום אאוט: האמירויות 94, סעודיה 90, טורקיה 85, איראן 80, ירדן, מצרים ולבנון 75.
ובכנות: האמירויות לפנינו, מקום 15 בעולם.
לא מושלמים. אבל ענייה ונחשלת? רחוק מזה.

Sources: UNDP Human Development Report 2025; OECD 2025; National Insurance Institute.

lines.line: This is a perfect quality of life. Israel is here.
Ninety-two out of a hundred, on the UN's Human Development Index. Health, education, income.
What's in the gap? Poverty: one in five Israelis.
Prices: fourth highest of thirty-eight rich countries.
And Israel is only twenty-seventh. Iceland is first.
Now zoom out. They picture Israel as a poor, backward place.
Poor and backward looks like this: around sixty-six, the UN's average for medium development.
The Emirates, ninety-four. Saudi Arabia, ninety. Turkey, eighty-five. Iran, eighty. Jordan and Egypt, seventy-five. Lebanon, seventy-five.
Only one neighbour is closer to utopia.
One honest catch: the Emirates beat us. Fifteenth in the world.
We're not perfect. We know it.
But poor and backward? Not even close.
